page: Microsoft Azure D32ls_v5 is a compute-oriented virtual machine belonging to the DLSv5 server family. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 16 physical Intel Xeon 8370C cores operating at 2.8 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, utilizing hyper-threading to provide two threads per core. Memory allocation is constrained to 64.0 GB, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. No local storage is bundled with this instance, though it is premium storage capable, and it does not include any GPU resources.

Benchmark evaluations place the D32ls_v5 in the average performance tier across most compute and memory workloads. The instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1682.0 and a multi-core score of 14191.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 36834.55. Image processing performance is a notable strength, ranking in the top 25% with a Geekbench score of 13651.0. Memory bandwidth tests show 1668.94 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 150.05 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads.

The primary tradeoff of the D32ls_v5 is its low memory density relative to its high core count, which limits its suitability for memory-intensive applications. This constraint is evident in large-scale language model inference; while text generation for a small 135M model is strong at 293.87 tokens per second, performance drops to a weak 6.66 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 70B model, and a poor 2.28 tokens per second for text generation. Consequently, this instance is best suited for compute-bound tasks with moderate memory footprints, such as software compilation, image processing, static web serving, and medium-scale database operations.
description: Microsoft Azure D32ls_v5 is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual machine from the DLSv5 family, featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz, this instance operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It lacks local storage and GPUs but supports premium external storage. Performance benchmarks generally fall within the average range, highlighted by a PassMark CPU score of 36834.55 and a strong Geekbench image processing score. Due to its low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU, the instance exhibits clear performance degradation on memory-heavy tasks like large LLM inference. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints, making it highly suitable for software compilation, image processing, and static web serving.
